name: How to Remove an Old Bathtub Safely and Efficiently

step.name: Step 1: Protect surrounding surfaces and clear the workspace
step.text: Cover the bathroom floor with heavy drop cloths, tape off doorway openings, and remove the vanity or toilet if they block your exit path. Protecting nearby finishes prevents accidental scratches or dents from heavy debris.

step.name: Step 2: Shut off the water supply and relieve line pressure
step.text: Turn off the dedicated bathroom valves or the main water shutoff to the house, then open the tub faucet to drain remaining water. Verifying the supply is completely dead keeps your workspace dry and safe.

step.name: Step 3: Remove tub hardware, spout, and overflow covers
step.text: Unscrew the handles, spout, and the overflow plate using standard hand tools to expose the underlying plumbing connections. Keep the removed pieces together in case you plan to reinstall matching trim later.

step.name: Step 4: Disconnect the drain shoe and overflow linkage
step.text: Access the plumbing behind the tub or through an access panel to unscrew the drain assembly from the main waste pipe. Double-check that the trap and waste line remain supported so you do not crack older fittings.

step.name: Step 5: Expose the tub flange by cutting back wall materials
step.text: Score and cut away at least six inches of drywall or tile directly above the tub lip to expose the hidden mounting screws or nails. Clearing this perimeter prevents torn drywall and lets the unit pull free cleanly.

step.name: Step 6: Remove mounting fasteners and dislodge the tub
step.text: Back out all screws or nails securing the flange directly to the wall studs. Pry the tub away from the framing using a sturdy pry bar, lifting it slowly to verify no remaining plumbing ties it down.

step.name: Step 7: Cut, break, or extract the tub from the space
step.text: Maneuver an acrylic or steel tub out intact, or carefully break a cast iron tub using safety goggles, ear protection, and heavy blankets. Once removed, vacuum up all debris and inspect the exposed subfloor for moisture.
